Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
759 AM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Ended the Frost/Freeze headlines this morning as temperatures
are quickly rising. The 2026 growing season has concluded for
all areas near and west of US-15.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and milder through Wednesday.

- 2) Much cooler conditions return for Thursday through 
     Saturday, along with chances for precipitation.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and milder through Wednesday.

Heights aloft will rebound later today while the pressure 
gradient relaxes substantially leading to slightly warmer 
temperatures and noticeable lighter winds this afternoon.

A dry cold front will then cross the area Monday, leading to 
gusty northwest winds returning. There isn't much of a thermal 
or moisture gradient/discontinuity with this front, so high 
temperatures will likely be similar to Sunday when combined with
downsloping effects.

Another sfc trough will move across the region Tuesday. 
Temperatures will be about 5 to 8 degrees above average as there
could be a warming surface wind out of the southwest. Highs 
will reach the middle 60s to lower 70s with upper 50s to near 60
in the mountains. Lows Tuesday night will drop into the upper 
30s to mid 40s. Once the front moves through, a surface high 
pressure will quickly build into and across the region for 
Wednesday. This will allow for temperatures to remain above 
average by a few degrees and the day to be dry. Highs in the 
middle to upper 60s with middle 50s in the mountains. The high 
quickly moves east by Wednesday night. Lows mid 30s to mid 40s. 
The colder temperatures could support some frost/freeze concerns
where the growing season continues mainly east of the Blue 
Ridge.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Much cooler conditions return for Thursday through 
Saturday, along with chances for precipitation.

Model guidance is in very good agreement that a very deep trough 
will dig southward across the Eastern half of the CONUS late in
the week. While there's good agreement that a longwave pattern 
with troughing in the East and ridging in the West will set up, 
there are still considerable differences with respect to the 
finer forecast details during that time, with several individual
lobes of vorticity interacting and then combining to ultimately
dig out the deeper longwave trough.

In terms of sensible weather, clouds will be on the increase on 
Thursday as the upper trough digs to our west. Despite the increase 
in cloud cover, temperatures are still forecast to be seasonable, 
with highs generally in the upper 50s and lower 60s. An area of low 
pressure is expected to form downstream of the digging trough, but 
there's still some spread with respect to where exactly it will form 
and how it will track. Some solutions (such as the 12z Euro) have 
the low tracking directly overhead on Thursday and then offshore 
Thursday night into Friday, while others (such as the 12z GFS) have 
the low forming to our south over the Carolinas and then tracking 
northeastward toward just east of the Delmarva. In most of these 
scenarios, precipitation would likely break out in the form of 
rain across much of the forecast area on Thursday.

In any of the above scenarios colder air will start to filter into 
the area from the north Thursday night into Friday. Depending on the 
ultimate track and strength of the low, some locations may 
transition over from rain to snow Thursday night into Friday. As is 
often the case, chances for snow will be greater as one goes higher 
up in elevation and further to the northwest.

If the absolute coldest solutions were to verify, many locations 
could see their first flakes of the season, although accumulations 
would still be unlikely at lower elevations with marginal 
temperatures in place. A more likely scenario is for precipitation 
to stay all rain at lower elevations with snow mixing in at the 
higher elevations. The Alleghenies will have the greatest chance for 
accumulating snow, but even there there's still considerable spread, 
due to the uncertainty in the finer scale details within the trough 
and the ultimate track/strength of the low.

Most guidance suggests that precipitation should begin to wind down 
by late Friday night, but a few solutions keep lingering light 
precipitation through much of the day Saturday. Either way, 
temperatures look to remain cool, with highs in the 40s to near 50.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
P6SM SKC and W winds 08g16kt. Some LLWS is possible tonight as
sfc winds decouple, but strengthen aloft. Stronger NW winds Mon
gusting up to 30 kt. Lighter winds Tue and Wed.

VFR conditions and light winds are expected during the day 
Wednesday. Winds will turn easterly on Thursday and then eventually 
northerly Thursday night. VFR conditions are expected through much 
of the day Thursday along with chances for rain. Sub-VFR conditions 
appear possible by Thursday night as ceilings start to lower.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds will continue to diminish through the day today. Have
canceled some SCAs where winds have already diminished. Winds
strengthen substantially on Monday in the wake of a dry cold
front. Have issued new SCAs for Monday, which may need to be
extended for some parts of the waters Monday night. 

Light and variable winds are expected over the waters on 
Wednesday. Wind will become easterly on Thursday and then 
northerly Thursday night. Small Craft Advisory level winds 
appear possible in northerly flow Thursday night.
